spec.title: PROP-059 — User-local application installers and launch points

status.comment: Native global application commands implemented and accepted with deterministic fixtures and actual isolated application installation, update and source-independent uninstall.

p.commands: vibe install -g PACKAGE, vibe update -g PACKAGE and vibe uninstall -g PACKAGE operate on exactly one fully qualified application package in the current user's Vibe settings root. The long spelling is --global. These routes run before project preparation and never mutate the current project's manifest, lock or dependencies. Ordinary invocations without this flag retain their existing semantics. The executable remains vibe; a second product-name alias is outside this change.

p.declaration: An app is a package-shaped, independently developed product: it may contain normal specs, prompts and code, and has [package] kind = "app" rather than a simultaneous [project] table. [application] supplies its stable local id and optional published command names. New installation declarations live only in nonempty [[installer_options]]; each option owns its installer method and user launch points. Package-author names, not heuristics, supply the displayed platform and installer names.

p.binary-ownership: ZIP and tar.gz payloads publish through the existing immutable generation and built-in management receipt under the owned application host. The actual selected payload root is recorded separately from hostRoot. Public runners, if declared, are owned by the existing opt/bin publication mechanism and must keep payload-relative resources working; unsupported unsafe wrapper forms are refused. An external shell, EXE or MSI installation may register a root outside Vibe, but that registration never grants Vibe recursive deletion rights over it.

p.ownership: The one user-local applications/index.json binds package identity, selected installer id/platform/architecture and method, owned hostRoot, actual appRoot, management entry, published runner ownership and authored launch points. Mutation uses the existing index lock and atomic save. A failed install or update does not replace the last ready binding. A registered external appRoot is used for resolution and never treated as a Vibe-owned directory to recursively remove.

p.installer-separation: Each [[installer_options.installation]].type declares exactly one installation type: shell, zip, tar_gz, exe or msi. This type is nested under an app package and does not add a package kind. Shell requires authored install and uninstall command strings and may declare an update command; Vibe invokes the host shell and streams the child output to the console, preserving machine-readable Vibe JSON by relaying child stdout to stderr in JSON mode. Apt, Homebrew and Winget are shell commands, not special kinds. ZIP/tar.gz carry an artifact source, SHA-256, optional payload subroot and optional runners; extraction rejects paths outside staging, links, special entries and conflicting names before publication. EXE/MSI carry a verified artifact source, SHA-256, expected appRoot, arguments and optional uninstall command; they execute only on Windows, with EXE direct execution and MSI through msiexec. All successful methods register in the same application index.

p.installer-options: The package author declares every visible [[installer_options]] row, each with stable id, nonempty name, platform id and authored display name, architecture id, one installation type and its own launch points. Only declared platform/architecture/installer rows are shown. Vibe auto-detects predefined platform ids linux, windows and macos and a matching host CPU architecture; other authored ids remain manually selectable. Installation accepts separate --platform, --arch and --installer selectors. Interactive selection visits platform, then architecture, then a named installer, placing a matching declared auto-detected row first. Unattended ambiguity reports a selection error. vibe app installers PACKAGE --json returns the complete versioned grouped list without executing an installer; update retains the prior selected id/platform unless the caller supplies a new selection.

p.force-and-hooks: Each installer option may declare pre_install and post_install shell commands. Pre runs before the selected installer; post runs after it succeeds and before the application index commits. Pre failure stops before installation. Post failure leaves the prior index binding intact and rolls back Vibe-owned archive publication; for an external shell/EXE/MSI installer Vibe reports that external payload state may already have changed. Global install/update --force chooses the shell method's required, separately authored force_install command, or the EXE/MSI method's authored force_arguments; a native method without forced arguments refuses the request. ZIP/tar.gz force may replace only files already owned by that app despite recorded hash drift and must retain rollback; it never claims an unowned destination or skips digest/path safety. Global uninstall --force chooses the shell method's required force_uninstall, the EXE/MSI method's authored force_uninstall (or refuses if absent), or removes only exact receipt-owned archive paths despite drift. Ordinary uninstall remains separate from forced uninstall.

p.launch-points: Each [[installer_options.launchers]] has a stable id, human name, executable template, optional description, args, working_directory and icon, and boolean terminal/default. IDs are unique within an option and at most one default is explicit. An absent or empty icon is normal. User launch points and published opt/bin runners are distinct. A successful update replaces the active launch-point set; paths are resolved against the current installation instead of persisted as stale physical paths.

p.launcher-paths: Launcher templates accept only $project_root, $app_root, $app_bin and $vibe_home, in braced or unbraced form, with $$ for a literal dollar. Expansion is one pass and never shell evaluation. Manifest paths may be relative to appRoot or derive an absolute path from a Vibe variable; literal absolute paths and parent traversal are refused. Executables and icons must resolve within registered appRoot or exact registered runners; working directories may resolve within appRoot or the selected projectRoot. Manifest args expand as scalar arguments; caller-supplied extra args remain literal. Without a selected project, a project-dependent point reports requires_project while other points remain listable and runnable.

p.launcher-operations: vibe app launchers PACKAGE --json reports a versioned, read-only list with package identity/version, templates, known resolved values, per-point availability and reason, and explicit default_launcher_id or null. vibe app run PACKAGE ID launches an exact current point; vibe app start PACKAGE optionally takes --launcher ID. Without ID, start chooses only an explicit default; otherwise attended terminal mode offers a choice and unattended mode reports selection_required, even for one nondefault point. Unknown ID, absent installation and unavailable point have separate diagnostics. Launch re-resolves and checks paths, invokes native programs with argument arrays, preserves synchronous exit status, and never installs or updates. Unsupported script or terminal modes fail explicitly.
